commits.message:
fix(projects, sharing): removal no longer depends on sharing; restore prefills; bound the relay's git calls (#199)

* fix(projects): removing a local project no longer depends on sharing

Removal deleted only this Space's copy, yet it asked the swarm who the repo
was shared with and blocked on the answer. The swarm answers 403 for a repo
nobody shared, so every never-shared GitHub project was stuck behind
"Sharing could not be verified", and a Space outside a sharing group was
told to get the owner to revoke everyone before deleting its own clone.

Removal now skips the membership check. Local safety checks, the
collaborator roster, the origin re-check and the relay's removal marker
(which stops the relay from cloning the folder back) are unchanged.
`members` stays in the removal response, always empty.

* feat(sharing): "Clone project" on a removed repo prefills the Add form

Inbox → Sharing lists a repo removed from this Space with a "Clone project"
button, which opened Manage's Add form empty although the repo was known.
It now passes the repository URL (https://<repo>.git, as the relay clones),
and the form suggests the folder name from it as it does for typed URLs.
The form is filled only when empty, so a draft in progress is kept, and
cloning still needs a click. Cache stamps are bumped for the changed modules.

* fix(sharing): bound the relay's git calls so a hang can't stall the loop

git fetch and git ls-remote ran with no timeout, so one hung network call
froze the relay for every repo until a restart. Every git call in git_ops
now has one: 300 s for fetch (a large pack can't resume, so it gets room),
60 s for ls-remote and 60 s for local reads. On a timeout the runner kills
git and its helpers, and the call fails like any other git error, so the
relay records it and retries on the next tick.

fetch and ls-remote also run with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 for that command
only, as clone already did: without credentials git fails at once instead
of waiting on a username prompt. With a credential helper nothing changes.

* docs(env): sharing bookmarks live in <state>/sharing/
commits.author: KrishBhimani

commits.message:
feat(quirq): show the full Space UI in ChatGPT/Codex sidebar, panel and chat (#200)

* feat(quirq): add MCP server with compact Space dashboard for ChatGPT/Codex

Bundle a local stdio MCP server with the quirq Codex plugin: read-only
tools for projects, project details and active sessions, a compact MCP App
dashboard with sidebar (global) and conversation (thread) entrypoints, a
demo mode, a packager for upload/marketplace ZIPs and hermetic tests.

* feat(quirq): show the full Space UI in ChatGPT/Codex sidebar, panel and chat

The plugin now renders the real Space UI (space_ui/, unmodified) inside the
ChatGPT desktop app instead of a separate dashboard:

- scripts/build_space_app.py bundles space_ui's markup, CSS, fonts and ES
  modules (esbuild) plus ui/space-bridge.js into one MCP App view,
  ui/space-app.html. The view is generated but committed, since the GitHub
  marketplace installs this folder from git; a freshness test fails while it
  is stale against its sources.
- ui/space-bridge.js does the MCP Apps handshake and replaces fetch for Space
  URLs: requests travel as space_api_read / space_api_write tool calls to the
  MCP server, which forwards them to the local Space. It also handles links
  (native opener, ui/open-link, copy fallback), deep links, hash routing and
  shares the visible page with the conversation (background context, "+ Chat").
- mcp/server.py: sidebar (global) and conversation panel (thread) entrypoints
  plus space_open for any Space page; app-only proxy tools with a path
  allowlist, header allowlist, size caps, no redirects and no server
  stop/restart/update; composer @-mentions with xo-space:// project, inbox and
  active-session resources; structured plugin settings; space_inbox and
  space_status; honest results for hosts that cannot display views.
- skills: onboarding skill (manifest onboardingSkill); start/install open Space
  in the app with the link as fallback and explain how long Space keeps running.
- Plugin version 1.5.0; EXTENSIONS.md documents design, build and limits.

* test(quirq): move plugin tests to tests/ and keep them out of the plugin

The tests shipped inside plugins/quirq (the ZIP and every marketplace install)
and the repo's own test run never executed them.

- tests/test_quirq_space_view.py (stdlib): the committed Space view is fresh
  against space_ui/ and the bridge; the upload ZIP contents (no tests/).
  Runs in every test run, where a space_ui change would make it stale.
- tests/test_quirq_plugin_server.py: the MCP server tests. They need the
  plugin's pinned mcp 1.x, so they skip (with the uv command) under mcp 2.x.
- tests/test_quirq_bridge.py runs tests/quirq/check_bridge.cjs when Node is
  available.
- Remove the manual smoke scripts check_ui.cjs (Playwright) and
  check_http.py; package_plugin.py no longer zips tests/.
- .gitattributes marks the generated ui/space-app.html as linguist-generated
  so GitHub collapses it in diffs.

* fix(quirq): enforce the proxy policy in the server, on the canonical route

The app-only visibility of space_api_read/space_api_write is a host hint,
not a boundary: a host that ignores it (Codex CLI, other MCP clients) lets
the model call the proxy, and Space trusts its requests as a local client.

- The server now refuses, for any caller: reading secret values; changing
  secrets, provider keys or the Composio key; jobs (they run local commands);
  Space chat; runtime config and restart; doctor actions; project sharing
  (share, revoke, apply, peers); deleting projects; server stop, restart and
  update. Everyday Space UI reads and changes keep working.
- Rules match the canonical route (decoded once as Space's server decodes it,
  slashes collapsed, no trailing slash), so percent-encoded variants such as
  /space/server/re%73tart no longer bypass the deny list. A path that only
  decodes into an allowed prefix is rejected.

* fix(quirq): forward only the routes the Space UI uses (default deny)

The proxy's deny list was default-allow: every Space route it did not name
was forwarded, including file read/write under $HOME (/api/files/*), skill
installs, connector token writes and /api/xo-projects-sync. Hosts may ignore
the app-only visibility hint, so the proxy is now an allowlist of exactly the
routes space_ui/js calls, matched on the canonical route:

- reads for every Space page (secrets: names only, never values);
- everyday changes: theme/branding, inbox status, project creation,
  connection settings and polling, telemetry sources.

Everything else (secret values, files, jobs, sharing, project deletion,
connector credentials, workspace config, server control, any future route)
is refused with "not available from ChatGPT; open Space in your browser".
Loading all 21 Space pages through the bridge against a live Space made 25
distinct requests; none is refused.

* docs(quirq): document the uv requirement for the MCP server

* refactor(quirq): remove demo mode from the plugin

QUIRQ_EXTENSION_DEMO made the MCP server answer from hardcoded sample
projects, sessions, todos and inbox items, and the compact dashboard had
its own ?demo=1 sample. Test scaffolding does not belong in what users
install, so both are gone: the plugin only ever shows real Space data.

The server tests now patch a small fake Space inside the test file, and
the real stdio protocol test checks the "Space unreachable" result instead
of sample data.

* chore: retrigger presubmit

* fix(quirq): run esbuild through utils.commands, not subprocess

The repo's one-executor rule (tests/test_command_executor.py) forbids
importing subprocess outside utils/commands. The build script now calls
utils.commands.run_sync, imported on use because the shipped plugin
contains the script but not the repo.

* docs(quirq): run Space through WSL when Codex runs on Windows

Space runs on Linux or macOS only. When Codex runs on Windows, the quirq
skill now runs the bundled scripts inside WSL (never Git Bash), converts the
plugin path with wslpath using forward slashes (backslashes are mangled on
the way into WSL), uses Linux workspace paths, and asks for wsl --install
when WSL is missing. Verified on Windows with Space already installed in WSL.

* build(quirq): rebuild the Space view from main's space_ui

main changed space_ui/ (#199); regenerate plugins/quirq/ui/space-app.html so
the freshness check matches the merged sources. See #226 for whether this
check should block space_ui/ changes.
commits.author: KrishBhimani

commits.message:
fix(quirq): keep scripts LF on Windows and report when Space is ready (#228)

* fix(quirq): keep scripts LF on Windows and report when Space is ready

Setting up XO Space from the Codex app on Windows took over five minutes:
the marketplace clone checked out the shell scripts with CRLF line endings,
which bash cannot run, and the start skill had the agent poll /health,
parse runtime-config and read config files by hand, one tool call at a time.

- .gitattributes: *.sh text eol=lf, so every checkout keeps runnable scripts.
- space.sh start runs the server as its child (still attached to the task),
  waits until discover.sh reports this checkout running, and prints one line,
  XO_SPACE_START {json}: running with base_url, repo_dir and roots, or
  exited/timeout pointing at the log. Then it waits on the server as before.
- quirq-start reads that line instead of verifying by hand.
- quirq-onboarding first identifies the system: Windows follows the quirq
  skill's "On Windows" section; macOS, Linux and WSL run the scripts directly.

* fix(quirq): rewrite discover.sh in existing clones and bump plugin versions

.gitattributes (eol=lf) applies only when git writes a file. Clones made on
Windows before it existed keep discover.sh with CRLF, because the file did not
change: the Codex marketplace clone still failed to run it. Touching both
identical copies (a comment) makes git rewrite them with LF on update.

Codex caches installed plugins by version, so the fixes reach existing
installs only with a new version: quirq 1.5.0 -> 1.5.1, the Claude plugin
(which shares discover.sh) 1.2.0 -> 1.2.1.
commits.author: KrishBhimani

commits.message:
fix(quirq): ask for approval before running wsl.exe on Windows (#229)

Codex's sandbox always blocks wsl.exe ("Access is denied",
Wsl/E_ACCESSDENIED). The skill did not say so, so the agent sometimes ran
the WSL path check inside the sandbox, read the denial as "WSL is missing"
and stopped without asking the user. The "On Windows" section now says to
run every wsl.exe command outside the sandbox from the first call, with the
user's approval, and when WSL counts as not installed. Bump quirq to 1.5.2.
commits.author: KrishBhimani

commits.message:
xo-doctor: never offer to move a live project's own history aside (#223)

When a project's .xo/project.json loses its pid (the identity sink then
mints a new one), has it changed, or is deleted, the project's earlier
history stays under projects/<old pid>/. The doctor listed that folder as
a leftover with a Move aside action, and move_aside() succeeded, even
though the leftover's recovered name was a project folder that still
exists.

A leftover whose last-known name matches a live project folder (exactly
or once normalised) is now runtime.identity_lost: no action, and a next
step that restores the old pid. FAIL when it is certainly the same
project (no usable pid, or its created_at predates the history's last
write; a re-minted pid keeps created_at), WARN when a new project may
only reuse the name. move_aside() re-checks the rule and refuses with
409 doctor_identity_lost. Damaged files inside the folder are grouped
under the finding, as they are under a leftover.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.author: Ankit Dwivedi

commits.message:
Keep only the previous command log when QUIRQ_COMMAND_LOG_ARCHIVE=false (#232)

* Keep only the previous command log on a release

A development checkout keeps every full commands.log in
inbox/activity/archive/, which nothing deletes. On a release that grows
without bound on machines nobody watches, so a release now keeps one
earlier generation instead: at 5 MB the log replaces commands.log.1, and
the two files never take more than about 10 MB.

A release is a checkout whose HEAD is exactly a vX.Y.Z tag (RELEASING.md),
asked once per process with `git tag --points-at HEAD`. When git cannot
answer (no checkout, no git) the install gets the bounded log.
QUIRQ_COMMAND_LOG_ARCHIVE=on|off overrides the checkout.

Until installs follow tags, every install is on a branch, so behaviour is
unchanged.

* Choose the command log archive with QUIRQ_COMMAND_LOG_ARCHIVE alone

Images ship without .git, so a git probe cannot tell a release from a
development build. Drop it: QUIRQ_COMMAND_LOG_ARCHIVE=true (the default)
keeps every full commands.log in inbox/activity/archive/ as before, and
false keeps only the previous one as commands.log.1.

* Tidy the command log rotation text and make the .1 helper private

The _iter_log_paths docstring and the Setup label said "archived" for
both modes; they now say rotated. _previous_command_log_path is only used
inside the module. A comment at the .1 replace records the cross-process
race the per-process lock cannot prevent.
commits.author: KrishBhimani

commits.message:
fix(codex): stop remote-control start hanging until the proxy 504s (#227)

* fix(codex): stop remote-control start hanging until the proxy 504s

`codex remote-control start` forks the app-server daemon and exits in a
few seconds, but run() waited in communicate() for its output pipe to
close, which a forked descendant can hold open. The request never
answered and the workspace proxy cut it at 60s with a 504.

- run(): new opt-in output_to_file captures into temp files and returns
  when the child exits; the codex remote-control adapter uses it.
- Action timeout 90s -> 45s, under the proxy's 60s limit, so a slow
  action reports its own timeout instead of a bare 504.
- _live_pid() reads daemon.pid (codex-cli 0.160+), then app-server.pid.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: RPC

* fix(codex): keep remote-control pair under the proxy's 60s limit

pair still answers inside the request but used the 180s action timeout,
so a slow or hung `codex remote-control pair` ran past the workspace
proxy's 60s limit and the user got a bare 504.

pair now runs under REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (45s): one deadline shared
by the wait for _action_lock and the CLI, so a queued pair answers
`busy` and a slow one `timeout` instead. CODEX_REMOTE_CONTROL_TIMEOUT
can shorten that budget but no longer lift it past the cap.

cryptography (pulled in by mcp -> pyjwt[crypto]) ships no Windows ARM

commits.message:
fix(doctor): report only what is true, and what the stores refuse (#230)

* fix(doctor): report documents that parse but their store can't use

The doctor judged a file healthy once it parsed and carried an accepted
schema number. A todos.json whose sessions is a list, a workitems.json
whose items is a list, a peers.json listing a user twice, or a
scheduler jobs.json whose jobs is a list all passed, while the stores
refuse them (todos and work items stop saving, collaborator requests
and project removal fail, no scheduled command runs). An inbox.json
whose items is not a list loads as empty, and the next write replaces
every saved item; that passed too.

Each of those stores now exposes its existing rule as a pure
shape_problem(document) and calls it where it validated inline, so its
behaviour and messages are unchanged. The Inbox store stays lenient;
its shape_problem only names what normalize_document would drop.

A new content check (after read) asks each owning store that question
for every file that parsed, and reports content.wrong_shape with the
store's reason as evidence and the catalog's wrong_shape/wrong_type
texts. Stores are imported inside the check, so a renamed function
costs only this check. The scheduler liveness check no longer goes
silent without a report when jobs or state is not an object.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(inbox): refuse to overwrite an inbox.json whose items would be lost

load_document read an inbox.json whose items is not a list, or whose
whole document is not an object, as an empty Inbox with ok=True. The
next refresh or change then wrote that empty Inbox back over the file,
so every saved item, seen and done mark and note was lost.

Such a file is now not ok, exactly like one that is not valid JSON:
reads still show an empty Inbox, refresh skips it, and modify refuses
with scope_unavailable (the message now says the items may be the
problem). The file is never rewritten. An inbox.json with no items key
yet is still a usable, empty Inbox.

The doctor's Inbox text follows: the wrong-type and wrong-shape cases
now say the Inbox shows empty and changes fail, instead of warning that
the next refresh overwrites it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(doctor): report saved commands that can't run while the watcher is off

The watcher is the only caller of scheduler.tick(), so with
QUIRQ_WATCHER_ENABLED=false an enabled saved command never runs. Both
the watcher and scheduler checks returned nothing in that case: on a
live server, a command five days overdue was reported as healthy.

The scheduler check now reports scheduler.not_running when the watcher
is off and enabled commands exist: WARN, or FAIL once one is already
past due, with the most overdue command as evidence. Turning the
watcher off is a setting a person may choose in Setup, so on its own it
is only an OK note (watcher.disabled), which the Health panel doesn't
show as a problem; the scheduler finding is not folded under it, since
a warning inside an OK row would be hidden.

Verified with a live server (watcher off, a command due since January):
scheduler.not_running FAIL naming the command.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(doctor): say whether XO refused the key, errored, or couldn't be reached

relay.unreachable told a person to check their network for every failed
poll: swarm_api.project_sharing.poll returned None for any failure and
the relay kept no status. On a live server with XO answering 401, the
usage check said "XO refused this Space's API key" while the relay
check, about the same 401, said "check this machine's network".

The swarm client gains poll_detailed() -> (body, status, offline); poll()
is now a thin wrapper with the same contract. The relay poller uses it
and records last_poll_status / last_poll_offline in its status snapshot
(additive), and its log line names the cause. The doctor maps one rule
for every XO caller (liveness.xo_failure): offline -> relay.unreachable,
401/403 or nothing to authenticate with -> relay.rejected, any other
answer -> relay.xo_error, unknown -> relay.failed, which claims no cause.

Usage reporting already recorded an inconclusive key check as
"unverified" with the HTTP status (or none when XO wasn't reached); the
doctor ignored it for 26 hours. It now reports usage.xo_error or
usage.unreachable.

Relay tests that mocked poll() now mock poll_detailed(). Verified on a
live server against a local fake XO: 401, 500 and no listener give
rejected, xo_error and unreachable for both relay and usage.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(doctor): tell an empty usage record from one that stops the watcher

A stats.json or sessions-augment.json holding the wrong JSON type got
one text for every case: "the watcher fails on this file on every tick".
On a live server that is true only for a value with content. The
watcher's sinks read `read_json(path) or {}`: an empty value ([], "", 0,
false, null) reads as no file and is replaced by totals counted from the
next activity, while a list or string with content makes the step raise
each time the project has new activity. That activity, and its timeline
lines, are then never recorded, even after the file is repaired
(verified live: 8 exchanges with stats.json = [1, 2] left the timeline
and totals unchanged, and repairing the file did not bring them back).

ReadResult gains empty_value for wrong_type, and a read finding looks
up the catalog's "wrong_type_empty" situation first. Both files now say
what actually happens in each case, and urge restoring a copy soon when
activity is being lost.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(storage): never read a device, FIFO or runaway file as a state file

With scheduler/jobs.json linked to /dev/zero, a live server allocated
about 1 GB on every watcher tick until MemoryError: the scheduler read
the path with read_text(), which never ends on a device. A FIFO at a
state path would make open() wait for a writer forever.

utils/safe_read.read_text_guarded() stats the path first and refuses
anything but a regular file (a link to one is followed, as before)
without opening it, opens with O_NONBLOCK and re-checks, and caps a
document at 50 MB. Its errors subclass OSError, so callers that already
treat an unreadable file as unreadable keep their behaviour. It is used
by the readers of state documents: storage.reader.read_json and
atomic_write's stamped-document reader (most stores), the scheduler,
the session index, the reading positions, the GitHub mirror, sharing
bookmarks, theme, branding, onboarding and the Inbox's empty-file check.
Append-only logs (timelines, run histories) grow by design, so they are
checked for their kind only, with no size cap. It lives in utils/
because the scheduler sits below services/.

Two tests that faked an unreadable file by patching Path.read_text now
patch the reader those modules use. Verified live: with jobs.json ->
/dev/zero the server's memory stays flat (82-89 MB over 30 s).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(doctor): report links, FIFOs and devices at state paths

The state walk kept only regular files, so a FIFO at inbox/inbox.json
or scheduler/jobs.json linked to /dev/zero was never judged and the
report said healthy (live test D4).

walk_files() can now collect every entry that is neither a regular file
nor a real folder (links to files or folders, FIFOs, sockets, devices),
still without opening or following any of them. For a known state path:
a FIFO or device is read.special; a link to one, or to a folder, gets
the same read finding with the link target as evidence; a dangling link
is shape.symlink (FAIL where losing the file is a FAIL); a link to a
real file is shape.symlink WARN, since every store saves with
os.replace() and so replaces the link with a regular file, and the
file it points to is judged as usual. Unknown entries stay OK notes,
and logs and credentials behind links are left alone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(doctor): correct the catalog where it misdescribes what the server does

An audit of every catalog text against the code that writes and reads
each file found five false claims and about twenty partial ones; the
user-visible ones were confirmed on a live server. Corrected:

- todos.json and cache/stats.json holding a list or string with content
  make their routes fail with HTTP 500 (`.get` on the value); an empty
  value reads as no document. Each case now says which, using the
  wrong_type_empty situation.
- cache/sessions/sessionslist.json and sessions-augment.json: nothing in
  the server reads them (Space-wide routes merge each project's index).
- projects.json is written through ChangeGate, so it is a change cache,
  not "replaced within seconds"; inventory behaviour updated.
- Change caches are also rebuilt at the next server start.
- An empty connection settings file is replaced with defaults on the
  next save; an empty or wrong-type accounts.json is rewritten by the
  next account lookup.
- Smaller corrections: what an Inbox refresh brings back; scheduler
  state needs the watcher; usage re-send needs sign-in and an accepted
  key; reading positions cover the agents that use that file; todo
  changes also rewrite session counters; session entries "usually"
  can't be resumed; a GitHub copy is rewritten by any poll and deleting
  it closes Inbox items only until each issue next changes; live
  activity with content fails its route; agent.json leaves the agent
  listed under its folder name; restoring .xo/ from git works only if
  the project commits it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(doctor): say how much was checked, so "Healthy" means checked

A report could read healthy while parts of the state were never looked
at: the walk stops at 50,000 entries, and a check can fail to run. A
big but healthy Space also carried a permanent FAIL for its size (live
test C1).

Every report gains a coverage block (additive): files seen, documents
read, unknown files, special entries, unreadable folders, whether the
walk was truncated, the walk limit, checks that couldn't run, and
complete. read.too_large becomes a WARN, since size isn't damage, and
is pinned so the per-check cap can never drop the row that says the
report is partial. The Health panel shows "Healthy (partly checked)"
instead of "Healthy" when coverage isn't complete, and adds the number
of files read (and "not every file was checked") to the check time; a
report from an older server without coverage renders as before. The view's
cache stamp and index.html's app.js stamp move together, and the plugin's
prebuilt plugins/quirq/ui/space-app.html is rebuilt.

Verified with a live server: 52,000 extra files give a WARN report with
complete=false; the panel's real badge code, run under node on live
reports, renders each case as described.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(doctor): show "partly checked" on the badge at any level

The Health badge said "Healthy (partly checked)" only when the level was
OK. A truncated walk always adds the read.too_large WARN, and a check
that couldn't run makes the level ERROR, so that text could never be
seen: on a live server with 52,000 extra files the badge read just
"WARN" while the report's coverage said complete=false.

"(partly checked)" now follows whatever the level is: "WARN (partly
checked)" in that case, "Healthy (partly checked)" if a future cause
leaves the level at OK. Stamps moved and the plugin's prebuilt UI is
rebuilt.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(install): only run from a checkout nobody else can change, and stop instead of resetting it (#236)

* fix(install): never adopt a shared temp dir as the checkout

The quirq.ai bootstrap saves install.sh to a temp file and runs it, and on
Linux that file usually sits in /tmp. resolve_repo_dir took any directory
holding server.py and requirements.txt as an in-place checkout, so files
another user left in /tmp were installed and run instead of xo-space. Both
probes (the script's own directory and the launch directory) now skip a
directory that is world-writable or owned by another user, and say why.

The port probe now exits 3 for "in use", so a crash in the probe (exit 1,
e.g. an ImportError) no longer reads as "Port 5002 is already in use".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UzFWDRUqzEGm8fntDTH9g1

* test(install): check the launch-dir probe through looks_like_checkout

The source-text test asserted the old inline "${LAUNCH_DIR}/server.py"
check, which the previous commit moved into looks_like_checkout.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UzFWDRUqzEGm8fntDTH9g1

* fix(install): trust a checkout by its real path, and stop instead of resetting it

The checkout probes now resolve the physical path (pwd -P) before any
check, so a symlinked checkout runs in place and macOS's /tmp link is
seen as the shared /private/tmp it points to.

A sticky world-writable folder (/tmp and the like) is never a checkout
and the install carries on in managed mode. Any other folder holding
server.py and requirements.txt must belong to the user, be writable by
nobody else (group write only for the owner's private group), carry no
ACL, and sit under folders nobody else can rename it out of. If it fails,
the installer stops with the reason and the fix (chmod go-w, setfacl -b,
or clone into a Linux folder on drives that keep no permissions) instead
of falling back to managed mode, which reset a world-writable clone to
upstream or nested a second clone in it.

The launch-dir probe adopts only a clone of the source repo, since
managed mode resets the tree, and root never adopts another user's folder
that way; root may still run another user's install.sh by path.

Harness cases cover symlinks, 0777 clones in all three launch forms,
drives without permissions, parents, group write, ACLs, another owner and
an unrelated project.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UzFWDRUqzEGm8fntDTH9g1

* fix(install): give the managed checkout the same trust check

The one-liner's own clone was never checked: under umask 000 (common on
WSL) it made a world-writable clone and ran it, and an existing managed
checkout that others could write to, or that another user owned, was
updated and run.

Now main drops other-write from the umask before creating anything, a
fresh clone is tightened with chmod -R go-w, and the managed checkout
passes checkout_trust_problem before any git command runs in an existing
one and again after the clone. Where chmod has no effect (WSL's /mnt/c,
FAT) that stops with the Linux-folder message INSTALLATION.md describes.

Also: repo_identity lowercases first and drops user and port from the
host only, and the filesystem check reads every layer findmnt lists.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UzFWDRUqzEGm8fntDTH9g1

* fix(install): say chmod -R go-w when the checkout itself is writable

Clearing the stop with plain chmod go-w left every file inside the
checkout writable by others. The message for the checkout now says
chmod -R go-w; a parent folder still gets plain chmod go-w, since only
its own bit matters.

commits.message:
test(inbox): pin retention's clock to the fixtures' date (#239)

InboxStoreTests stamps its items with a fixed NOW (2026-09-10) while
store.modify runs retention on the wall clock. Since 2026-10-10 that
date is more than DONE_TTL_DAYS in the past, so an item stamped NOW and
then auto-closed was pruned by the same write, and two tests found no
item where they expected one.

setUp now wraps store.apply_retention so it defaults to NOW. An explicit
now still wins. No production code changes.

Stop bundling the xo-projects skill; default the projects root to ~ (#249)

* chore(skills): stop bundling the xo-projects skill

Remove .agents/skills/xo-projects/ and empty BUNDLED_SKILLS. The boot-time
installer (install_xo_skills) stays, so a repo skill can be bundled again by
adding its folder and its name; with the list empty the step installs nothing.

The tests that read the skill's reference files go with it; the inbox view-name
check that also validated the store and feeders is kept without the doc text.
INSTALLATION.md no longer offers "ask your coding agent" to create a project.

* feat(layout): default the projects root to the home directory

XO_PROJECTS_ROOT now falls back to ~ instead of ~/xo-projects, in
project_layout and the doctor's copy of the default. The Space UI clone
fallback, the openclaw/hermes troubleshoot xo.json default, the manifests'
workspace_dir and the docs that named the root follow. The plugin Space view
is rebuilt for the sharing_data.js change.

Only runs with XO_PROJECTS_ROOT unset change: install.sh still defaults to the
directory it was run from. With the root at ~, every non-hidden folder in the
home directory is listed as a project and gets a .xo/ from the watcher.
